title: My expectations were high but i was still quite disappointed
body:
I really appreciate the concept of Habitica, and I believe gamification could greatly help me in achieving my goals. However, I feel a bit disappointed because the minigames aren't very engaging and seem disconnected from the tasks. When I complete a task, I only feel satisfaction from the task itself, as I don't find the pets or boss fights particularly interesting. While these features help keep me somewhat accountable, they don't add much excitement.

I suggest adding an extra step between completing a task and earning rewards, such as a short text-based adventure that players can experience after finishing a task. Introducing more minigames, perhaps similar to the Discord meme game, could enhance the fun factor, as it aligns with the style Habitica aims for. Additionally, crafting systems for creating better weapons and armor, and allowing pets to provide buffs, could add depth to the game.

For the boss fights, incorporating more prominent character synergies that are effective against certain bosses would make them more strategic and engaging. Overall, I think Habitica has tremendous potential to be useful, but in its current state, it feels similar to other to-do list apps. That being said i still use habitica and find it useful

title: Fantastic - bordering on life-changing
body:
I could not run my life without this app. That's the shortest possible way I can describe my experience with it after using it for three years. It's cute and fun and its structure grasps something that few other task management apps have been able to replicate. Separating habits, periodical tasks and one-off to-do's is simple but like many simple things, it took a long time for somebody to do it! Now that Habitica has, though, there's no going back for me. 

Recent updates have introduced some annoying bugs but the developers are responsive and hard-working. I'm sure they'll iron them out quickly as they always do. The glitches are worth putting up with, especially because you can use Habitica in a browser, where there are few glitches. The browser use means that you can have it open in a tab on your computer at work, in class or anywhere else and not have to worry about using your phone.

This thing is just so versatile. It only loses a star because some of its current bugs are a bit of a hassle. Let me repeat myself, though: they are worth putting up with for this gem of an app.

title: Review v2.1.2 (2/XII/2018)
body:
This app has come a long way since its inception. Version 2.0 was the biggest leap forward for this app, having introduced a whole lot more stability and functionality than previously. 

It's true that v2.0.0 was still buggy, but upon reflection, it was hard to expect them to get it perfect...because they aren't as big as Google or Facebook. Big mistakes were bound to appear left, right and centre.

While the issues with synchronisation are still there, it's pretty good with conflict resolution between tasks as far as I can tell. The app is much more stable and there is a fair amount of functionality regarding feeding pets and starting Quests. (Still need to fix up the bug where it takes multiple refreshes to view the quest details and buttons without distortion.)

All in all, this app is a good supplement to the main website, but they do need to step up their game if they want their game to capture the essence of productivity in us all.

- @dispatch009

title: Lots of Room for Improvement
body:
Hopefully creators will read this, I am genuinely interested to use the app to its fullest potential and will be interested to support the app after a few more weeks of using it.

My thoughts on first glance:

Ideas:

1. Changing the title for ‘Dailies’, i think something like Recurring Tasks or just Tasks would make more sense considering there’s the option to have Daily, Monthly and Yearly reminders.

2. Need more details for Reminders. Currently the reminders for tasks only come in time (e.g. 8:00am) but tasks that continue for a few days might need more advanced detail such as reminders in multiple times during the day (morning, afternoon, night). Or needing to be reminded a few hours, days or minutes before a task.

3. Option to colour code tasks when they’re created.

4. Option to add custom tags.

Bugs:

1. The Character inside the Profile Picture is a little off-centre

2. Slide bar to delete tasks take too long to delete the task, or loading problem when task is being deleted.

title: App of the year!
body:
Habitrpg has been the most useful app I have downloaded all year. As a sufferer of anxiety, I often battle with a consistent buzzing in my head which makes me unable to remember things I should do in a day. When the day finishes, I go to bed with a sense of unfulfilment, wondering if I forgot anything today. This brought me to a place where I would lose track of my studying and lose sleep because of last minute assignments. The stress of this was causing health complications. 

Ever since I got habitrpg, I have been able to keep a step-by-step record of my tasks, and good habits are much more inviting and memorable when I can add points for them. I check my to-do list and my dailys every night and I get a sense of peace because I know what I have done that day. Habitrpg is not only a fantastic program to boost your good habits and prune the bad habits, but it is also an amazing way to keep track of a stressful life.

title: I Don't Write Reviews
body:
Ever. So why am I starting now? Because I use Habit RPG frequently and have always been frustrated by the lack of features in their app.

Never again will I have to say that.

For those people who don't know: Habit RPG is a task-keeper; a to-do-list and a tiny bundle of sprite based, quest induced joy. This is their app.

It supports all the features available at the full Habit RPG website and has been cleverly formatted to, very successfully, work on your phone or other iOS device with minimal effort on your part.

The app itself feels well developed and polished, additionally it is hands down my favourite To-do-list on iOS.

Cheers. 

DIE CHECKLIST. DIE.
